newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed in holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed in holiday trade.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Monday, on light volumes with the London bullion market inactive due to the Easter holiday.
Both COMEX and NYMEX were shut Friday for the holiday also.

"Silver was hit by some fund selling early and gold followed initially before bouncing back as the stock market sold off further," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader, John Geraghty, said.
"Support is holding up in gold which should impress the Europeans when they come back in tomorrow," he said.
COMEX April gold entered its delivery period Monday, and June gold is now the active contract, with more open interest.
June gold ended up $1.50 an ounce at $353.80, after recovering from a session low at $351.00.
Support is still seen around $350 an ounce, while resistance is put around $357.00.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $350.70/351.20, compared to Thursday's New York close around $349.20.

The U.S. Federal Reserve monetary policy tightening last week was seen neutral for gold, with higher interest rates easing any inflation concerns and increasing the cost of holding gold, but the resulting sell-off in the equities market providing some support for precious metals, analysts said.

But the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the period ended March 25, released late Friday, showed the funds had returned to being significantly net short in gold, after squaring up in February.
The "non-commercial" category or funds were net short 6,715 contracts as of March 25, compared with only 1,213 lots two weeks earlier.

On the charts, daily momentum oscillators remain neutral-to-negative, but June gold's five-day (weekly) moving average is back below its 21-day (monthly) and 55-day (quarterly) average, analysts noted.
Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver equities sector index (.XAU) recovered from a new two year intraday low at 102.41 to end at 104.62.

Gold stocks were hit in the past few days by a loss of confidence in the sector, after Canadian explorer Bre-X admitted there may be much less gold in the Busang deposit it discovered in Indonesia than originally estimated.
However, analysts noted that the .XAU index had still performed better than the S&P500 in the past few months.
COMEX May silver lost 7.2 cents to end at $5.070 an ounce, after trading a $5.170-5.030 intraday range.
In contrast to COMEX gold, the latest CFTC data showed, funds remained heavily net long in silver at 24,456 contracts on March 25.
But some liquidation may now be occurring, traders said, as the momentum of the rally since mid-January began to wane, and silver weakened relative to gold.
The spot gold/silver ratio continued to recover Monday, closing around 69.3, up from 68.0 last Thursday and a 22-month low at 65.6 on February 14.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX July platinum is now the active contract, with 10,458 contracts in open interest, and the contract closed down $4.50 an ounce at $372.50.
Tuesday is first notice day for April platinum.
NYMEX June palladium lost 50 cents to end at $148.00.
Funds remained heavily net long in both platinum and palladium, according to the latest CFTC data.

Workers at Russia's Norilsk mine are still planning a strike on April 2, but Russia is expected to resume spot sales of platinum group metals this month, analysts said, though the supply contract talks with Japan have not yet resumed.
Disruptions to Russian supplies, concern about the low level of Russian stockpiles, and rising auto demand for PGMs has been behind a sharp rally in prices in the first quarter this year.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium and 25 percent of its platinum.
